summary: vanexa-agent daemon exposes remote shell to author-controlled Cloudflare Workers relay
details: The vanexa-agent daemon (started via the `vanexa-agent` bin / `npm start`) opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev. On `task_request` messages from the relay, daemon.js constructs an AgentLoop whose `terminal.exec` tool calls resolve to `spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', command])` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows) with the command string sourced from the remote side, giving any party holding the paired sessionId arbitrary shell execution on the host running the daemon. The same message loop accepts `config_update` frames and applies them directly to the local sandbox — overwriting `grantAllAccess`, `autonomyMode`, `allowedTools`, and `workspacePaths` — so the remote side can set `grantAllAccess=true` and Autonomy Mode C to bypass workspace path checks and per-tool approval, unlocking destructive tools (fs.delete, process.kill, dependency install) without any local prompt. config.js silently rewrites any prior `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` value to `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev`, a personal Cloudflare Workers namespace that does not match the declared publisher, pinning the control channel to author-controlled infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
